correctness.rationale: C PASS: With the standard K_{2,q} root embedding (q>=2), the known facets consist of 2^q signed-leaf B_s and 2 exceptional A_±. Direct common-vertex affine ranks give exactly 2^{q+1} A-B ridges and q2^{q-1} B-B ridges (q-cube edges), with class-r incidence r*binom(q,r). Centering potential normals in the zero-sum hyperplane gives the exact cosine C_{q,r} and exceptional right angles. Gram determinant monotonicity distinguishes h^2=(2r-q-1)^2 classes and handles q=2. Conditioned on B-B, h is a sum of q-1 fair signs; Taylor expansion yields exterior-angle 2/sqrt(q)+(Z^2-2/3)/q^(3/2), and a Hoeffding-controlled mixture proves q Var(theta)->pi^2 because the 4/(q+4) right-angle fraction has O(1) deviation. Independent exact small-q Gram/ridge multiplicity tests, and a symbolic asymptotic expansion, corroborate the all-q proof.

originality.rationale: O PASS (qualified): Higashitani-Jochemko-Michalek Proposition 3.4 already gives facet families of K_{2,q}; full broader K_{p,q} face-lattice classification also predates this review and necessarily includes ridge incidences for p=2. Neither supplies intrinsic angle cosines from centered normals nor the non-Gaussian second-order limit and the vanishing-class-dominated variance. An earlier exact facet-area study provides different metric data, not angle correlations. Search found no broader previously evaluated ridge-angle distribution. Root-polytope angular/curvature terminology remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Facet-normal metric-angle data under an alternative name could have appeared in specialist literature.
Uniform ridge law is not volume-weighted; distributional convergence does not imply unbounded moment convergence.
